reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full EnrollmentResponse StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate, and the shared behavior context. I treated the aggregate as prior context only. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was considered as background and not scored because the assigned artifact is `EnrollmentResponse`, not `Resource` or `DomainResource`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `EnrollmentResponse` is FMM 0/trial-use, so the compatibility burden is weak. That softens concern for additive fields and terminology cleanup, while still leaving room to preserve low-cost migration aids for financial workflow implementations.

overall.oneLineConclusion: EnrollmentResponse has no unavoidable resource-level R4-to-R6 migration program; the only meaningful compatibility work is per-change terminology/tooling migration for `outcome` and optional downgrade handling for `candidate`.

reasoning.thesisMd: `EnrollmentResponse` keeps the same resource identity and preserves its local R4 content model. No local R4 element is removed, renamed, made mandatory, retargeted, or constrained in a way that rejects ordinary R4 instances. The resource-level migration shape is therefore low material change, not a redesign.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: Forward R4-to-R6 migration is mostly structural no-op. R6 adds optional `EnrollmentResponse.candidate`, so old instances do not need backfill. `EnrollmentResponse.outcome` remains the same optional `code` element and the compared local code strings remain `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial`; the migration work is updating required-binding canonicals, generated enum names, terminology caches, and conformance tests. R6-to-R4 downgrade or round-trip support needs a policy for preserving populated `candidate`.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because no broad resource migration program is already unavoidable, compatibility should be evaluated per change rather than dismissed as dominated by a redesign. The current changes do not justify a major preservation campaign, but low-cost transition aids for the `outcome` terminology change still have practical value.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: For `candidate`, no less-breaking base R6 design is needed for the R4-to-R6 direction; omitting the optional element would fail the R6 goal of representing the enrollment subject or group. For `outcome`, a less-disruptive transition could retain or alias the old `remittance-outcome` canonical, publish an additional binding, or provide an explicit ConceptMap. That is useful migration support, but retaining a remittance-named primary binding for enrollment semantics has real terminology-design tradeoffs, especially on FMM 0 content.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: There are no direct operation, search, or HTTP behavior findings assigned to `EnrollmentResponse`. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain important base-platform context, but they are not EnrollmentResponse-specific resource migration drivers under the review rules.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is `No` and the shape is `low-material-change`. I am slightly less dismissive on compatibility leverage: the aggregate chose `no-special-break-avoidance-needed`, while the stable resource shape and the `outcome` canonical churn make `preserve-compatibility-per-change` the better posture. This does not turn either local finding into a high-priority revisit.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The main uncertainty is terminology intent: no official R4-to-R6 diff, terminology expansion, or ConceptMap was supplied for the move from `remittance-outcome` to `enrollment-outcome`. The resource-level conclusion is still high confidence because the structural comparison is direct and the code lists match in the local packages.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional EnrollmentResponse.candidate with no native R4 equivalent
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is an additive optional R6 element, so it does not make R4 instances invalid in R6 and does not drive a resource-level migration program. It still matters for R6-to-R4 downgrade and round-trip policy because a populated candidate may carry business-relevant patient or group enrollment context that base R4 cannot represent.

findingConsiderations.title: EnrollmentResponse.outcome required binding changed from remittance-outcome to enrollment-outcome
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only local change with meaningful forward migration work. The instance code strings appear unchanged, so it is not an old-valid/new-invalid instance break, but terminology-aware validators, generated enums, caches, and rules keyed to the ValueSet or CodeSystem canonical need migration. That supports per-change compatibility attention rather than a major resource migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource operation removal can affect generic clients for many resource types, but it is not specific to `EnrollmentResponse` and should be handled by the base Resource/API behavior review rather than counted as an EnrollmentResponse migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is important base validation behavior, but its affected resource is `Resource`; it does not alter the EnrollmentResponse StructureDefinition migration shape or create an EnrollmentResponse-specific behavior finding.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared search-parameter metadata can affect clients that search EnrollmentResponse like any other resource, but the finding is owned by shared Resource/DomainResource search behavior and is not direct evidence of an EnrollmentResponse resource-level redesign.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: For the `outcome` binding change, publish or verify transition guidance such as an explicit ConceptMap, alias, additional binding, or note confirming that the four R4 `remittance-outcome` codes map unchanged to R6 `enrollment-outcome`.
If R6-to-R4 downgrade or round-trip support is required, define a standard extension or IG mapping for populated `EnrollmentResponse.candidate`; otherwise document that omission is lossy.

Keep shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search behavior remediation in the base behavior reviews; do not inflate EnrollmentResponse into a resource-level migration program because of those shared findings.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 EnrollmentResponse diff or ballot rationale was supplied.
No local ConceptMap or official ValueSet expansion was available for the outcome binding replacement; equivalence is inferred from local complete CodeSystem concept lists.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context and not scored as direct EnrollmentResponse findings.
